body.text: oṃ namaḥ sarvajñāya ||
body.translated_text: Oṃ, homage to the Omniscient One!

body.text:
evaṃ mayā śrutam ekasmin samaye bhagavān* śrāvastyāṃ viharati sma jetavane anāthapiṇḍadasyārāme mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena sārdham ardhatrayodaśabhir bhikṣusahasraiḥ | tadyathā āyuṣmatā cājñātakauṇḍinyena āyuṣmatā ca mahānāmnā āyuṣmatā ca revatena āyuṣmatā ca vakkulena āyuṣmatā ca śāripu[treṇa āyuṣmatā ca] pūrṇena maitrāyaṇī[putreṇa] ca śrāvakaniyutaiḥ | te sarve yena bhagavān yena ca jetavanaṃ vihāraṃ tenopasaṃkrāntā bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya bhagavataḥ puratas tasthur dvātriṃśatā bodhisatvasahasraiḥ | tadyathā sahacittotpādadharmacakrapravartanena ca bodhisatvena mahāsatvena anikṣiptadhureṇa ca bodhisatvena mahāsatvena maitreyeṇa ca bodhisatvena mahāsatvena avalokiteśvareṇa ca bodhisatvena mahāsatvena mahāsthāmaprāptena ca bodhisatvena mahāsatvena | evaṃpramukhair dvātriṃśatā bodhisatvasahasraiḥ | te sarve yena bhagavān yena ca jetavanaṃ vihāraṃ tenopasaṃkrāntā
bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya bhagavataḥ puratas tasthuḥ | atha khalu bhagavān pūrvāhṇakālasamaye nivāsya pātracīvaramā[traḥ] śrāvastīṃ mahānagarīṃ piṇḍāya prāviśat* | atha bhagavān āyuṣmantam ānandam (Asv 104) āmantrayate sma | gacchānanda pātraṃ cakrikaṃ śikyamānaya | athāyuṣmān ānando bhagavataḥ śrutamātreṇa pātraṃ cakrikaṃ śikyaṃ bhagavate upanāmayām āsa | athāyuṣmān ānando bhagavataḥ kṛtāñjalipuṭo bhagavantaṃ gāthābhir adhyabhāṣata |
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time, the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) was dwelling in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in the <s>Jetavana</s> (Jeta's Grove), in the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, together with a great assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks) — twelve and a half thousand monks. Namely, with the venerable <s>Ājñātakauṇḍinya</s>, the venerable <s>Mahānāman</s>, the venerable <s>Revata</s>, the venerable <s>Vakkula</s>, the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the venerable <s>Pūrṇa Maitrāyaṇīputra</s>, and ten million <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples). They all approached the <s>Bhagavān</s> and the <s>Jetavana</s> monastery, bowed their heads at the <s>Bhagavān's</s> feet, and stood before the <s>Bhagavān</s> — together with thirty-two thousand <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Namely, with the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Sahacittotpādadharmacakrapravartana</s> (He Who Turns the Dharma Wheel at the Very Arising of the Thought), with the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva Anikṣiptadhura</s> (He Whose Burden Is Not Set Down), with the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva Maitreya</s>, with the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara</s>, with the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta</s>. With these and others at their head, thirty-two thousand <s>bodhisattvas</s>. They all approached the <s>Bhagavān</s> and the <s>Jetavana</s> monastery, bowed their heads at the <s>Bhagavān's</s> feet, and stood before the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, in the morning time, having dressed and taken his bowl and robe, entered the great city of <s>Śrāvastī</s> for alms. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Go, <s>Ānanda</s>, bring the bowl, the spinning wheel, and the carrying sling.' Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having merely heard the <s>Bhagavān's</s> words, offered the bowl, the spinning wheel, and the carrying sling to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with palms joined together, addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> in verses:

body.text:
yadā tvaṃ praviśasi piṇḍapātika
  vimocaye tvaṃ bahavaṃ hi prāṇinām* /–MS: vimocayeyaṃ ... uttārayeyaṃ
uttāraye tvaṃ bahavaṃ satvā
  narakabhayāj jātijarāmahābhayā //
body.translated_text: When you enter for alms-food, you liberate many living beings; you ferry across many beings from the fear of hells, from the great fears of birth and old age.

body.text:
saṃsāraduḥkhakalilā mahābhayād
  {vimocayeyaṃ tava lokanāyakāḥ} /

children.translated_text: The greatly powerful one, worthy of the best offerings,
having liberated many beings
mired in the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s>, from the great fear,
having liberated them, he shall come again.

body.translated_text: Those mired in the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), from the great fear — I would liberate them, O <s>Lokanāyaka</s> (Leader of the World)!

body.text:
athāyuṣmān ānando bhagavata imā gāthā bhāṣitvā tūṣṇīṃ sthito 'bhūt* | atha bhagavān* śrāvastyāṃ mahānagaryāṃ nātidūre sthito 'bhūt* | atha te sarve gavākṣatoraṇaniryūhakā [hiraṇya]mayāḥ sphaṭikamayā rūpyamayāḥ prādurabhūvan* | tathā śrāvastyāṃ ma[hānagaryāṃ] mahāntaṃ janakāyaṃ saṃsthito 'bhūvan* | atha sa janakāyaḥ saṃśayajāto babhūva ko hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayaḥ nagarasya śubhanimittaṃ prādurabhūt* | mā cedaṃ nagaraṃ bhasmapralayaṃ syāt* | atha tatra janakāye anekavarṣaśatasahasriko (Asv 105) jīrṇo vṛddho mahallakaḥ puruṣaḥ saṃsthito 'bhūt* | atha sa puruṣas taṃ janakāyaṃ samāśvāsayann evam āha | mā bhaiṣur bhoḥ kulaputrāḥ | asminn eva pṛthivīpradeśe jetavanaṃ nāma vihāraḥ | tatra śākyamunir nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ
ca buddho bhagavān* | so 'yaṃ śrāvastīṃ mahānagarīṃ piṇḍāya prāviśat* | tasyāgamanakālasamaye idaṃ śubhanimittam abhūt* | atha sa janakāyas taṃ jīrṇakaṃ puruṣaṃ kṛtāñjalir [evam āha] | yat tasya bhagavatas tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya gu[ṇavarṇasamudīraṇa]samaye idaṃ śubhanimittam abhūt* | dṛṣṭamātrasya tasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya kīdṛśaḥ puṇyābhisaṃskāro bhaviṣyati | atha sa jīrṇakapuruṣas taṃ janakāyaṃ bhagavato guṇavarṇasamudīraṇatayā gāthābhir adhyabhāṣata |
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having spoken these verses to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, stood in silence. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> stood not far from the great city of <s>Śrāvastī</s>. Then all the windows, arched gateways, and turrets appeared made of gold, crystal, and silver. And in the great city of <s>Śrāvastī</s>, a great multitude of people had assembled. Then that multitude of people became filled with doubt: 'What is the cause? What is the condition? An auspicious sign has appeared for the city. May this city not be destroyed by a conflagration!' Then in that crowd there stood a man who was aged, old, and decrepit, having lived for many hundreds of thousands of years. Then that man reassured the crowd and spoke thus: 'Do not be afraid, good sons of noble family! In this very region of the earth there is a monastery called <s>Jetavana</s>. There dwells a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Śākyamuni</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, a Knower of the World, an unsurpassed charioteer of men to be tamed, a Teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Bhagavān</s>. He has entered the great city of <s>Śrāvastī</s> for alms. At the time of his arrival, this auspicious sign appeared.' Then the crowd, with palms joined, spoke to the aged man: 'At the time of praising the qualities of that <s>Bhagavān Tathāgata Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, this auspicious sign appeared. What manner of meritorious formation will there be from merely seeing that <s>Tathāgata Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One?' Then the aged man addressed the crowd, praising the qualities of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, in verses:

body.text:
yo lokanāthasya hi nāmu yaḥ śruṇe
  saṃsāraduḥkhā vinimuktu so naro /
apāyagāmī na kadāci bheṣyate
  svargaṃ ca so yāsyati śīghram evam* /

children.text: yo lokanāthasya hi nāmu yaḥ śruṇe
children.translated_text: Whoever hears the name of the <s>Lokanātha</s>,
firm in his resolve, through many billions of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons),
the greatly powerful <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One), of great soul,
through inconceivable billions and tens of millions of <s>kalpas</s> —

body.translated_text: Whoever hears the name of the <s>Lokanātha</s> (Protector of the World), that person is freed from the sufferings of <s>saṃsāra</s>; he shall never become one bound for the lower realms; and he shall quickly go to heaven thus.

children.translated_text: that <s>bodhisattva</s> stood firm for as many aeons as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> (Ganges);
never shall he go to a lower rebirth or fearful state.

children.text: yo lokanāthasya hi nāmu yaḥ śruṇe
children.translated_text: Whoever hears the name of the <s>Lokanātha</s>,
he shall never become one bound for the lower realms.
For inconceivable billions and tens of millions of <s>kalpas</s>,
he shall always be a king, a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch).
Whoever upholds the name of the <s>Lokanātha</s> —

children.text: yat kiṃci pūrvaṃ sada pāpu yat kṛtaṃ
children.translated_text: whatever evil was formerly done in the past,
all of it shall quickly come to destruction.
<s>Śakra</s>, the lord of gods, of great power,
for inconceivable billions and tens of millions of <s>kalpas</s> —
he shall go to <s>Sukhāvatī</s> (Land of Bliss), the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field),
and that <s>bodhisattva</s>, seated in cross-legged posture,
with <s>Brahma's</s> voice, a sweet voice, a melodious voice,
they shall be so for billions of thousands of years.

body.text:
apāyagāmī na kadāci bheṣyate
  yo lokanāthasya hi nāmu dhārayet* /
body.translated_text: He shall never become one bound for the lower realms — whoever upholds the name of the <s>Lokanātha</s>.

body.text:
atha sa jīrṇakaḥ puruṣo janakāyaṃ bhagavato guṇavarṇam udīrayitvā tūṣṇīṃ sthito 'bhūt* | atha bhagavān pūrveṇa nagaradvāreṇa śrāvastīṃ mahānagarīṃ praviṣṭo 'bhūt* | tatra ca nagaradvāre dvādaśakoṭyaḥ padmānāṃ prādurabhūvan* | teṣu ca padmeṣu dvādaśakoṭyo bodhisatvānāṃ paryaṅkaniṣaṇṇāḥ (Asv 107) prādurabhūvan prāñjalayaḥ | atha bhagavataḥ praviṣṭamātreṇa śrāvastyāṃ mahānagaryāṃ navanavatikoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi satvānāṃ sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātau pratiṣṭhāpitāni caturaśītisatvakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇy ābhiratyā lo[kadhāto]r akṣobhyatathāgatasya buddhakṣetraṃ pratiṣṭhāpitāni |
atha bhagavān ā[nandena saha nagarā]valambikāyā dārikāyā gṛhe samāgato 'bhūt* | atha bhagavān nagarāvalambikāyā dārikāyā gṛhe cakrikaṃ kaṭakaṭāpayām āsa | atha sā dārikā taṃ cakrīśabdaṃ śrutvā saṃśayajātābhūt* | ko hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayaḥ | mama gṛhe na kadācit piṇḍapātika āgato 'bhūt* | atha sā nagarāvalambikā dārikā śūnyākāragṛhe niṣaṇṇā aśrukaṇṭhī rudantī paridevantī sthitābhūt tīkṣṇadhāram asiṃ gaveṣantī paridevantī rudantī sthitābhūt* | atha [sā] dārikā śūnyākāragṛhe niṣaṇṇā paridevantī aśru[kaṇṭhī] rudantī gāthābhir adhyabhāṣata |
body.translated_text: Then the aged man, having praised the qualities of the <s>Bhagavān</s> to the crowd, stood in silence. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> entered the great city of <s>Śrāvastī</s> through the eastern city gate. And at that city gate, twelve <s>koṭis</s> (ten millions) of lotuses appeared. On those lotuses, twelve <s>koṭis</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s> appeared, seated in cross-legged posture, with palms joined. Then, merely upon the <s>Bhagavān's</s> entrance into the great city of <s>Śrāvastī</s>, ninety-nine <s>koṭi-niyuta-śatasahasras</s> (trillions) of beings were established in the world-realm of <s>Sukhāvatī</s>, and eighty-four <s>koṭi-niyuta-śatasahasras</s> of beings were established in the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> of <s>Tathāgata Akṣobhya</s> in the world-realm of <s>Abhirati</s> (Supreme Delight). Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, together with <s>Ānanda</s>, arrived at the house of the girl <s>Nagarāvalambikā</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> sounded his spinning wheel at the house of the girl <s>Nagarāvalambikā</s>. Then that girl, hearing the sound of the spinning wheel, became filled with doubt: 'What is the cause? What is the condition? Never before has an alms-seeker come to my house.' Then the girl <s>Nagarāvalambikā</s>, sitting in an empty inner room, with tearful throat, weeping and lamenting, stood there seeking a sharp-edged sword, lamenting and weeping. Then the girl, sitting in the empty inner room, lamenting, with tearful throat, weeping, spoke in verses:

body.text:
aho bata duḥkhu daridrake gṛhe
  varaṃ mama maraṇu na cāpi jīvitam* /

children.translated_text: What use is life to me in these affairs,
when I am afflicted with bodily suffering?
... without refuge, with no support for the hereafter.

children.text: anāthabhūtā aham adyameva yadyaivāhaṃ jāta daridrake gṛhe //
children.translated_text: I am without a protector this very day, since I was born into a poor house.

body.translated_text: Alas, how wretched in this poor house! For me, death would be better than life.

body.text:
atha sa nagarāvalambikā dārikā śūnyākāragṛhe [niṣaṇṇā] imā gāthā bhāṣitvā tūṣṇīṃ sthitābhūt* |
atha śuddhavāsakāyiko devaputro 'ntarīkṣagataḥ sthitaś cintayati sma | paśyec ced imāṃ bhagavān* | anekaduṣkarakoṭiniyutaśatasahasracīrṇacaritaḥ sa śākyamunis tathāgato nagarāvalambikāyā dārikāyā gṛhe sthito 'bhūt* | atha śuddhavāsakāyiko devaputraḥ śatasahasramūlyaṃ muktāhāraṃ gṛhītvā śatarasabhojanapiṭakaṃ gṛhītvā kāśikāni vastrāṇi gṛhītvā yena nagarāvalambikāyā dārikāyā gṛhaṃ tenopasaṃkrānto 'bhūt* | atha śuddhavāsakāyiko devaputro nagarāvalambikāṃ dārikām evam āha | prāvara dārike imāni kāśikāni vastrāṇi imāny anekaśatasahasramūlyāny ābharaṇāni | prāvṛtya cedaṃ śatasahasramūlyaṃ muktāhāraṃ gṛhītvā imaṃ śatarasabhojanapiṭakaṃ gṛhītvā bhagavantam upanāmaya | atha sā dārikā tāni kāśikāni vastrāṇi prāvṛtya śatasahasramūlyaṃ muktāhāraṃ gṛhītvā taṃ śatarasabhojanapiṭakaṃ gṛhītvā yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntā | upasaṃkramya
bhagavantam upanāmayati sma | atha bhagavāṃs tāṃ nagarāvalambikām evam āha | pariṇāmaya tvaṃ dārike yathā pariṇāmitaṃ vipaśyiśikhiviśvabhukkakutsundakanakamunikāśyapaprabhṛtibhiḥ sadbhis tathāgatair arhadbhiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhaiḥ | anto bhaviṣyati strībhāvād anto bhaviṣyati daridragṛhāt* | atha sā dārikā taṃ piṇḍapātaṃ pariṇāmayitvā (Asv 109) bhagavantam upanāmayām āsa | anena piṇḍapātakuśalamūlena mā kasmiṃścid daridragṛhe upapadyeya |
atha sā nagarāvalambikā dārikā taṃ piṇḍapātaṃ pariṇāmayitvā bhagavate datvā svagṛhagamanam ārabdhā | atha bhagavāṃs tāṃ nagarāvalambikāṃ dārikām evam āha | pratinivartasva dārike | pūrvajātinidānaṃ samanusmarāmi | tad ahaṃ pa[rikīrta]yiṣyāmi | atha sā dārikā pratinivṛtya sarvāṅgapraṇi[pātena] bhagavantaṃ prapatitā | atha sā nagarāvalambikā dārikā bhagava[ntaṃ gā]thābhir adhyabhāṣata |
body.translated_text:
Then the girl <s>Nagarāvalambikā</s>, seated in an empty house, having spoken these verses, remained silent.
Then a <s>devaputra</s> (divine being) of the <s>Śuddhavāsa</s> (Pure Abodes) class, standing in the sky, thought: 'If only the Blessed One could see her!' That <s>Śākyamuni Tathāgata</s>, who had practiced conduct through tens of millions of <s>koṭis</s> of austerities, stood in the house of the girl <s>Nagarāvalambikā</s>. Then the <s>Śuddhavāsa devaputra</s>, taking a pearl necklace worth a hundred thousand, taking a food-basket of a hundred flavors, and taking <s>Kāśi</s> garments, approached the house of the girl <s>Nagarāvalambikā</s>. Then the <s>Śuddhavāsa devaputra</s> said to the girl <s>Nagarāvalambikā</s>: 'Put on, O girl, these <s>Kāśi</s> garments [and] these ornaments worth many hundreds of thousands. Having put them on, take this pearl necklace worth a hundred thousand, take this food-basket of a hundred flavors, and offer [them] to the Blessed One.' Then that girl, having put on those <s>Kāśi</s> garments, taking the pearl necklace worth a hundred thousand, taking that food-basket of a hundred flavors, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, she made the offering to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One said to that <s>Nagarāvalambikā</s>: 'Dedicate [this merit], O girl, as was dedicated by the noble <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly enlightened Buddhas — <s>Vipaśyin</s>, <s>Śikhin</s>, <s>Viśvabhuk</s>, <s>Kakutsunda</s>, <s>Kanakamuni</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, and others. There shall be an end to [your] female state; there shall be an end to [birth in] a poor household.' Then that girl, having dedicated that alms-food, offered [it] to the Blessed One [with the aspiration]: 'By this root of merit from alms-food, may I not be reborn in any poor household.'
Then the girl <s>Nagarāvalambikā</s>, having dedicated that alms-food and given it to the Blessed One, began to return home. Then the Blessed One [addressed] that <s>Nagarāvalambikā</s>—

children.translated_text: Certainly by my previously done <s>karma</s> (action)
I was born in a poor household.
Show compassion to me who am suffering;
turn back the guardians of hell!
Show compassion to me who am suffering —
I have been born in the state of a woman, O Leader!
You, O Lord of the World, from old age, disease, and grief —
free me who am suffering!
Be [my] protection, [my] refuge, [my] final resort;
free me who am suffering!

children.text: kṛtaṃ hi nātha praṇidhiṃ tvayā hi
children.translated_text: For you, O Lord, have made the vow (<s>praṇidhi</s>):
'Whatever beings there are here in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> —'
'Those who stand in the ten directions —
all beings I shall make happy.'
'And I shall liberate all from the ocean of suffering.'
Be [my] protection, [my] refuge, [my] final resort!

children.text: tvayaṃ hi nātha mayi mocayī jagat*
children.translated_text: You, O Lord, shall liberate the world through me.
Certainly by my previously done <s>karma</s>
I was born in a poor household.
Be [my] protection, [for] me who am suffering!
You, O Lord, are the liberator from old age and disease;
be [my] protection, O foremost one, endowed with accumulated virtues!

children.text: na cā kariṣye punar eva pāpaṃ
children.translated_text: And never again shall I do evil —
[not] that which I [now] experience as these sufferings!
Having compassion ... foremost of beings,
be [my] protection, [my] refuge, [my] final resort!
Whatever beings there are here in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> —

children.text: nāmaṃ ca vai dhāraya paśca kāle //
children.translated_text: hold [my] name in the future time!
After the <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> [of the Buddha], in the future time,
there will be destruction of the teaching.

children.text: yat kiṃci pāpaṃ tadapūrva yat kṛtaṃ
children.translated_text: Whatever evil was done before by me —
all that shall quickly come to exhaustion!

body.text: atha sā nagarāvalambikā dārikā bhagavantaṃ gāthā bhāṣitvā pu[nar api] gṛhagamanam ārabdhā | atha bhagavān tāṃ nagarāvalambikāṃ (Asv 111) [dārikāṃ kala]viṅkarutasvaranirghoṣeṇaivam āha | pratinivartasva [dārike pūrvajātinidānaṃ sa]manusmarāmi tad ahaṃ parikīrtayiṣyāmi | [atha sā dārikā] pratinivṛtyaivam āha |
body.translated_text: Then the girl <s>Nagarāvalambikā</s>, having spoken verses to the Blessed One, again began to return home. Then the Blessed One addressed that girl <s>Nagarāvalambikā</s> with a voice like the song of the <s>kalaviṅka</s> bird, saying: 'Turn back, O girl! I recall the cause from your former births — I shall proclaim it.' Then that girl, having turned back, said:

children.translated_text: 'Proclaim today, O Guide of the World,

children.text: ya[d yat kṛtaṃ] pāpa sadā sudāruṇam* /
children.translated_text: whatever terrible evil was always done [by me]!
'Certainly terrible evil was done by me,
by which I was born in a poor household.'
'You are the caravan-leader of the entire world;
free me here from the state of a woman!'
'Be [my] protection, [my] refuge, [my] final resort!'
'I shall always be grateful to the Leader!'
'Let me hear this <s>Dharma</s>-guide —
one who follows it never falls into the lower realms.'
'May [it] purify the <s>karma</s> done by me [as it was done]!'
'Be [my] protection, [my] refuge, [my] final resort!'

body.text:
asaṅgajñānī varalokanāyaka
  vandāmi nātha śaraṇaṃ kṛtāñjalī //
body.translated_text:
'O knower of non-attachment, best Leader of the world —
I worship you, O Lord, [my] refuge, with palms joined!'

body.text:
atha bhagavāṃs tāṃ dārikām evam āha | bhūtapūrvo dārike atīte 'dhvani asaṃkhyeyaiḥ kalpaiḥ ratnaśikhī nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān* | tena (Asv 112) khalu punaḥ samayena padmāvatī nāma rājadhāny abhūt* | tena khalu punaḥ samayena padmāvatyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ padmaprabho nāma gṛhapatir abhūt* | tasya padmaprabhasya gṛhapates tvaṃ [duhi]tābhūḥ | tena khalu punaḥ samayena grāmanagaranigamajanapadeṣu piṇḍapātiko bhikṣuḥ piṇḍapātāyāvatarati | yadā tvadgṛham āgato 'bhūt tadā tvaṃ dārike piṇḍapātaṃ gṛhītvā gṛhān niṣkrāntā punar eva praviṣṭābhūḥ | na cāhaṃ muṇḍitaśiraso 'dhanyasya piṇḍapātaṃ dāsyāmi | tena karmopacayena tvayā dārike dvādaśa kalpasahasrāṇi punaḥ punar daridragṛhe duḥkhāny anubhūtāni | ekena tvayā
dārike kuśalamūlena bodhivyākaraṇaṃ pratilapsyase | yat tvayā tasya bhikṣo rūpaliṅgasaṃsthā na dṛṣṭā bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ dārike anāgate 'dhvani acintyair aparimāṇaiḥ kalpair nagaradhvajo nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān* loke | atha sā dārikā bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtvaivam āha | kīdṛśaṃ bhagavan mama buddhakṣetraṃ bhaviṣyati yatraivāhaṃ buddho bhaviṣyāmi | bhagavān āha | aparimitaguṇasaṃcayā nāma sā buddhakṣetraṃ bhaviṣyati | yādṛśī ca sā sukhāvatī lokadhātuḥ tādṛśaṃ tad buddhakṣetraṃ bhaviṣyati | paryaṅkaniṣaṇṇā āryopapādukā bodhisatvā bhaviṣyanti | īdṛśaṃ tad buddhakṣetram* | (Asv 113)
atha ca sā dārikā tuṣṭā udagrā āttamanāḥ pramuditā prītisaumasyajātā svagṛhagamanam ārabdhā | atha bhagavāṃs tāṃ dārikām evam āha | tvaṃ dārike saptame divase kālaṃ kariṣyasi | kālaṃ kṛtvā | pūrvasyān diśi magadhaviṣaye rājā ajitaseno nāma | tasya rājño 'jitasenasya antaḥpurasahasram asti | tasya khalu punā rājño 'jitasenasya putro janiṣyase | eṣa eva tava paścimo garbhavāso bhaviṣyati |
atha bhagavān paścimakena nagaradvāreṇa śrāvastyā mahānagaryā niṣkrānto yena jetavanaṃ vihāras tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | athāyuṣmān ānando bhagavantaṃ dūrata evāgacchantaṃ dṛṣṭvā pādau śirasābhivandya triḥpradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavantaṃ gāthābhir adhyabhāṣata |
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One said to that girl: 'Long ago, O girl, in the past, innumerable <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) ago, there was a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, perfectly enlightened Buddha named <s>Ratnaśikhin</s>, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of men, teacher of gods and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One. At that time, there was a royal capital named <s>Padmāvatī</s>. At that time, in the royal capital <s>Padmāvatī</s>, there was a householder named <s>Padmaprabha</s>. You were the daughter of that householder <s>Padmaprabha</s>. At that time, an alms-gathering monk descended to the villages, towns, market-towns, and districts for alms. When he came to your house, you, O girl, having taken the alms-food, went out of the house and then went back in [saying]: "I will not give alms-food to this shaven-headed, wretched one!" By that accumulation of <s>karma</s>, O girl, for twelve thousand <s>kalpas</s> you experienced suffering again and again in poor households. But by one root of merit, O girl, you shall receive the prophecy of awakening (<s>bodhivyākaraṇa</s>). Because you did not see the true form and appearance of that monk — you, O girl, in the future, after inconceivable and immeasurable <s>kalpas</s>, shall become a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, perfectly enlightened Buddha named <s>Nagaradhvaja</s>, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of men, teacher of gods and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One in the world.' Then that girl, having circumambulated the Blessed One three times, said: 'What, O Blessed One, will my Buddha-field be like, where I shall become a Buddha?' The Blessed One said: 'That Buddha-field will be named <s>Aparimitaguṇasaṃcaya</s> (Accumulation of Immeasurable Qualities). And just as that <s>Sukhāvatī</s> world-realm [is], so shall that Buddha-field be. The <s>Bodhisattvas</s> there will be noble ones, seated cross-legged, spontaneously born —'

children.translated_text: 'Of golden complexion, adorned with excellent marks,
bearing the form of thirty-two marks —'
'When you have come as an alms-gatherer,
having liberated all beings here —'
'You shall establish all beings in happiness;
the power of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) for the entire world has been accomplished by you.'
'That excellent alms-food, O Leader of the World —'
'The world has been liberated by you from fear!'

body.text:
ye bodhisatvā iha jambudvīpe
  sarve ca mārgaṃ tava darśayanti /

children.translated_text: After the complete <s>parinirvāṇa</s> [of the Teacher], in the future time,
may they uphold this <s>sūtra</s> described by the <s>Buddha</s>.

body.translated_text: All the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> here in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> show your path;

children.translated_text: After your complete <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, in the future time,
there will be the destruction of the teaching;
may [they] uphold this jewel of a <s>sūtra</s>, this method.

body.text:
athāyuṣmān ānanda imā gāthā bhāṣitvā bhagavantaṃ triḥpradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavataḥ puratas tasthau | atha bhagavān āyuṣmantam ānandam āmantrayate sma | gacchānanda gaṇḍīm ākoṭaya | te śrāvakāḥ paribhokṣyanti piṇḍapātam* | athāyuṣmān ānando bhagavantam āmantrayate sma | kīdṛśaṃ bhagavan gaṇḍīśabdasya kuśalamūlaṃ bhaviṣyati | bhagavān āha | śṛṇu ānanda gaṇḍīśabdasya kuśalamūlaṃ parikīrtayāmi | ye kecid ānanda gaṇḍīśabdaṃ śroṣyanti teṣāṃ pañcānantaryāṇi kṛtyāni parīkṣayaṃ yāsyanti | avaivartikās te bhaviṣyanti kṣipraṃ cānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbhotsyante | ānanda āha | kīdṛśaṃ bhagavaṃs taiḥ satvaiḥ kuśalamūlam avaropitam* | bhagavān āha | śṛṇu ānanda ye satvāḥ paścime kāle paścime samaye mama parinirvṛtasya saddharmavipralope vartamāne saddharmasyāntardhānakālasamaye grāmanagaranigamajanapadarāṣṭrarājadhānīṣu
ye satvā [vā] araṇyāyatane gaṇḍyākoṭanaśabdaṃ śroṣyanti namo buddhāyeti kariṣyanti teṣāṃ pañcānantaryāṇi karmāṇi parikṣayaṃ (Asv 115) yāsyanti | īdṛśāny ānanda gaṇḍīśabdasya kuśalamūlāni | athāyuṣmān ānandaḥ śāntapraśāntena gaṇḍīm ākoṭayate sma | atha tena gaṇdīśabdena sarve te mahāśrāvakāḥ sannipatitā abhūvan* | yathā yathā āsane niṣaṇṇāḥ piṇḍapātaṃ paribhuñjante sma | atha tatraiva śrāvakamadhye nandimitro nāma mahāśrāvakaḥ sannipatito 'bhūt* sanniṣaṇṇaḥ | atha bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ nandimitraṃ mahāśrāvakam āmantrayate sma | gaccha tvaṃ nandimitra mahāśrāvaka pūrvasyān diśi magadhaviṣaye rājño 'jitasenasya kalyāṇamitraparicaryāṃ kuru | atha nandimitro mahāśrāvako bhagavantam evam āha | na bhagavan* śakṣyāmas taṃ pṛthivīpradeśaṃ gantum* | durāsadās te satvāḥ | te māṃ jīvitād vyavaropayiṣyanti | atha bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ
taṃ nandimitraṃ mahāśrāvakam evam āha | na te satvās te śakṣyante bālāgram api kampayituṃ prāgeva jīvitād vyavaropayitum* | atha nandimitro mahāśrāvakaḥ pratyūṣakālasamaye suvarṇavarṇaṃ vastraṃ prāvṛtya yena pūrvasyān diśi magadhaviṣaye rājño 'jitasenasya rājadhānī tenānukrānto 'bhūt* | atha rājā ajitasenas taṃ nandimitraṃ mahāśrāvakaṃ dṛṣṭvā tuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajāto 'bhūt* | atha rājñājitasenena amātyaḥ preṣito 'bhūt* | gacchainaṃ bhikṣum ānaya | tadā so 'mātyo yena nandimitro mahāśrāvakas (Asv 116) tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | atha so 'mātyo nandimitraṃ mahāśrāvakam evam āha | āgaccha mahāśrāvaka bhikṣo rājā te ājñāpayati | atha nandimitro mahāśrāvako 'mātyam evam āha | mama rājñā kiṃ kāryaṃ mama rājā kiṃ kariṣyati | athāmātyo yena rājājitasenas tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | taṃ rājānam ajitasenam evam āha | na ca sa bhikṣus tava pārśve āgacchati
| atha rājñājitasenena pañcāmātyaśatāni preṣitāni | na ca sa bhikṣū rājño 'jitasenasya pārśvam āgacchati | atha sa rājā svakenaivātmabhāvena yena sa nandimitramahāśrāvakas tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya kṛtāñjalir evam āha | āgaccha bho bhikṣo mama rājadhānīṃ praviśa | atha rājā ajitaseno dakṣiṇahaste taṃ bhikṣuṃ gṛhītvā svakāṃ rājadhānīṃ praviṣṭo 'bhūt* | atha rājñājitasenena nandimitrasya bhikṣoḥ siṃhāsanaṃ dattam abhūt* | atha rājājitaseno bhadrapīṭhake niṣadya taṃ nandimitraṃ mahāśrāvakam evam āha | kutra tvaṃ bhikṣo gacchasi | ko hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayaḥ | atha nandimitro mahāśrāvako rājānam ajitasenam evam āha | ye kecid bhikṣupravrajitās te sarve bhikṣāhārāḥ piṇḍapātam avacarantaḥ paribhuñjanti | atha rājā ajitasenas taṃ nandimitraṃ mahāśrāvakam evam āha | paribhuṅkṣva mama gṛhe piṇḍapātam* | yāvajjīvaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ pradāsyāmi | yadi te bhikṣo mama
svamāṃsena kāryaṃ svamāṃsaṃ dāsyāmi | atha nandimitro mahāśrāvako rājānam ajitasenaṃ gāthābhir adhyabhāṣata | (Asv 117)
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having spoken these verses, circumambulated the <s>Bhagavān</s> three times and stood before the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Go, <s>Ānanda</s>, strike the <s>gaṇḍī</s> (wooden gong). The <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples) will partake of their alms-food.' Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'What, <s>Bhagavān</s>, will be the wholesome root of the <s>gaṇḍī</s>-sound?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Listen, <s>Ānanda</s>, I shall proclaim the wholesome root of the <s>gaṇḍī</s>-sound. Whoever, <s>Ānanda</s>, will hear the <s>gaṇḍī</s>-sound — for them the five <s>ānantarya</s> (heinous) deeds will be exhausted. They will become <s>avaivartika</s> (non-retrogressing), and they will quickly attain unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>).' <s>Ānanda</s> said: 'What wholesome root was planted by those beings?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Listen, <s>Ānanda</s>. Those beings who in the final time, in the final period, when the destruction of the true <s>Dharma</s> is underway after my <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, at the time of the disappearance of the true <s>Dharma</s> — in villages, cities, market-towns, districts, kingdoms, and capital cities — those beings who hear the sound of the striking of the <s>gaṇḍī</s> in a forest hermitage and utter "<s>Namo Buddhāya</s>" (Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>) — for them the five <s>ānantarya</s> (heinous) deeds will be exhausted. Such, <s>Ānanda</s>, are the wholesome roots of the <s>gaṇḍī</s>-sound.' Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> struck the <s>gaṇḍī</s> calmly and peacefully. Then by that <s>gaṇḍī</s>-sound, all those great <s>śrāvakas</s> assembled. As they were seated in their places, they partook of alms-food. Then, right there among the <s>śrāvakas</s>, a great <s>śrāvaka</s> named <s>Nandimitra</s> assembled and sat down. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the great <s>śrāvaka</s>, the venerable <s>Nandimitra</s>: 'Go, <s>Nandimitra</s>, great <s>śrāvaka</s>, to the eastern direction, to the <s>Magadha</s> region, and serve as a spiritual friend (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>) to King <s>Ajitasena</s>.' Then <s>Nandimitra</s>, the great <s>śrāvaka</s>, said thus to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'I am unable, <s>Bhagavān</s>, to go to that region of the earth. Those beings are difficult to approach. They will take my life.' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> said thus to the great <s>śrāvaka</s>, the venerable <s>Nandimitra</s>: 'Those beings will not be able to disturb even a single hair-tip, let alone take your life.' Then <s>Nandimitra</s>, the great <s>śrāvaka</s>, at the time of early dawn, having wrapped himself in a golden-colored robe, set out in the eastern direction toward the capital of King <s>Ajitasena</s> in the <s>Magadha</s> region. Then King <s>Ajitasena</s>, having seen that great <s>śrāvaka</s> <s>Nandimitra</s>, became pleased, elated, delighted, joyful, and filled with delight and happiness. Then King <s>Ajitasena</s> sent a minister: 'Go, bring that <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk).' Then that minister approached the great <s>śrāvaka</s> <s>Nandimitra</s>. That minister said thus to the great <s>śrāvaka</s> <s>Nandimitra</s>: 'Come, great <s>śrāvaka</s>, O <s>bhikṣu</s>, the king commands you.' Then <s>Nandimitra</s>, the great <s>śrāvaka</s>, said thus to the minister: 'What business have I with the king? What will the king do for me?' Then the minister approached King <s>Ajitasena</s> and said thus to King <s>Ajitasena</s>: 'That <s>bhikṣu</s> does not come to your presence.' Then King <s>Ajitasena</s> sent five hundred ministers. But that <s>bhikṣu</s> still did not come to the presence of King <s>Ajitasena</s>. Then the king himself went to where the great <s>śrāvaka</s> <s>Nandimitra</s> was. Having approached, with palms joined, he said: 'Come, O <s>bhikṣu</s>, enter my capital.' Then King <s>Ajitasena</s>, having taken that <s>bhikṣu</s> by the right hand, entered his own capital. Then King <s>Ajitasena</s> gave a lion-throne to the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Nandimitra</s>. Then King <s>Ajitasena</s>, having sat on a fine seat, said thus to the great <s>śrāvaka</s> <s>Nandimitra</s>: 'Where are you going, O <s>bhikṣu</s>? What is the cause? What is the reason?' Then <s>Nandimitra</s>, the great <s>śrāvaka</s>, said thus to King <s>Ajitasena</s>: 'All those who have gone forth as <s>bhikṣus</s> subsist on alms-food, wandering about for alms and partaking of them.' Then King <s>Ajitasena</s> said thus to the great <s>śrāvaka</s> <s>Nandimitra</s>: 'Partake of alms-food in my house. I shall provide alms-food for as long as you live. If you need my own flesh, O <s>bhikṣu</s>, I shall give my own flesh.' Then <s>Nandimitra</s>, the great <s>śrāvaka</s>, addressed King <s>Ajitasena</s> with verses:

children.translated_text: "I shall eat that food which you give —
fine food and drink, the supreme nourishment of flavors.
You shall become liberated from the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions);
you have obtained the rarely obtained human birth.
Rarely obtained is the teaching of the Leader;
supreme faith and devotion are exceedingly rare.
Those <s>bhikṣus</s> who have gone forth in the teaching —
exceedingly rare is the teaching of the Leaders.
Exceedingly rare is the sight of the best of <s>Sugatas</s>;
homage to you, O <s>Buddha</s> of great power!
Homage to you, O great sage, [embodiment of] <s>Dharma</s>!
Homage to you, noble one skilled in [destroying] the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions)!

body.text:
namo 'stu te sarvajarapramokṣaṇāt*
  namo 'stu te mārganidarśanāryam* //
body.translated_text:
Homage to you, for liberation from all aging!
Homage to you, noble one who shows the path!

body.text:
namo 'stu te mārgapathasya darśakaṃ
  namo 'stu te bodhipathasya darśakam* //
body.translated_text:
Homage to you, shower of the way of the path!
Homage to you, shower of the path to <s>bodhi</s> (awakening)!"

body.text: atha nandimitro mahāśrāvako rājānam ajitasenaṃ bhagavato guṇavarṇam udīrayitvā tūṣṇīṃ sthito 'bhūt* | atha rājānam ajitasenaṃ taṃ nandimitro mahāśrāvako gāthābhir adhyabhāṣata |
body.translated_text: Then the great <s>śrāvaka</s> <s>Nandimitra</s>, having praised the <s>Bhagavān's</s> virtues to King <s>Ajitasena</s>, stood in silence. Then the great <s>śrāvaka</s> <s>Nandimitra</s> addressed King <s>Ajitasena</s> with verses:

body.text:
sudurlabhaṃ bhikṣu tathaiva darśanaṃ
  sudurlabhaṃ tasya bhaveya darśanam* /

children.translated_text: Those who give a gift to the <s>bhikṣusaṃgha</s> (community of monks) —

children.text: na tasya yakṣā na ca rākṣasāś ca //
children.translated_text: neither <s>yakṣas</s> nor <s>rākṣasas</s>,

body.translated_text:
"Exceedingly rare is the sight of a <s>bhikṣu</s>;
exceedingly rare would be the sight of him.

children.translated_text: nor <s>pretas</s>, <s>kumbhāṇḍas</s>, or great <s>nāgas</s>
ever create obstacles for them.
Those who give gifts to the <s>bhikṣusaṃgha</s> —
exceedingly rare for them is the gain of human birth.
One who [sees] the rare sight of the state of a <s>bhikṣu</s>,
exceedingly rare [even] in inconceivable hundreds of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) —
one who upholds the name of the Lord of the World,
for inconceivable billions of <s>kalpas</s>,
will never go to the lower realms of suffering.
One who sees such a king of <s>bhikṣus</s> —
for that one there will be no lower realm of suffering;
one who sees such a king of <s>bhikṣus</s>.
A spiritual friend (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>), a guide upon my path —
he has come [here]; [I am] one who goes for alms-food.
One who gives alms-food to him —
they shall be freed, they shall not fear old age, disease, or death.

body.text:
kleśā vinirmukta sadā tu bheṣyati
  te tasya dāsyantiha piṇḍapātam* //
body.translated_text:
Freed from the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) they shall ever be;
they shall give alms-food to him here."

body.text:
atha sa rājā ajitaseno nandimitraṃ mahāśrāvakaṃ guṇavarṇam udīrayitvā tūṣṇīṃ sthito 'bhūt* | atha nandimitro mahāśrāvako (Asv 119) rājānam ajitasenam evam āha | evam astu mahārāja bhuñje piṇḍapātaṃ tava gṛhe | atha rājā ajitasenaḥ khādanīyena bhojanīyena taṃ nandimitramahāśrāvakaṃ santarpayati sma |
atha nandimitramahāśrāvako rājānam ajitasenam evam āha | kiṃ tava mahārāja asmin pṛthivīpradeśe udyānabhūmir asti | rājā āha | asti mahāśrāvaka udyānabhūmir mama ramaṇīyā suśobhanā | nandimitra āha | gacchāmy ahaṃ mahārāja | tām udyānabhūmiṃ prekṣe | rājā āha | gaccha nandimitra | udyānabhūmiṃ prekṣasva | atha nandimitramahāśrāvako yena rājño 'jitasenasyodyānabhūmis tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | atha tatrodyānabhūmau ye udyānaguṇās te sarve santīti | yā graiṣmikyaḥ puṣkariṇyas tāḥ śītalajalaparipūrṇā yā vārṣikyas tā nātyuṣṇā nātiśītalajalaparipūrṇāḥ | tāś ca puṣkariṇyaḥ suvarṇasopānasaṃcchannā divyā ramaṇīyāḥ | ye ca jāṃbūpakaparibhogaguṇās te sarve santīti | adhimuktakacampakāśokamucilindapāṭalasumanāsaugandhikapuṣpāṇi santīti | (Asv 120) ye tiryagyonigatāḥ pakṣiṇaḥ śukaśārikācakravākamayūrakokilādayas te nānārutāni kurvanti sma | atha tatraiva udyānabhūmau
suvarṇavarṇāḥ suvarṇatuṇḍāḥ suvarṇapakṣāḥ suvarṇapādāḥ pakṣiṇāḥ prādurbhūtāḥ | te sarve buddhaśabdaṃ niścārayanti | atha nandimitramahāśrāvako yena rājño 'jitasenasya rājadhānī tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | atha rājā ajitasenas taṃ nandimitraṃ mahāśrāvakam evam āha | āgatas tvaṃ mahāśrāvaka | dṛṣṭodyānabhūmiḥ | nandimitra āha | dṛṣṭā mayodyānabhūmī ramaṇīyā suśobhanā | atha nandimitraṃ mahāśrāvakaṃ rājā ajitaseno gāthābhir adhyabhāṣata |
body.translated_text:
Then King <s>Ajitasena</s>, having praised the virtues of the great <s>śrāvaka</s> <s>Nandimitra</s>, stood in silence. Then the great <s>śrāvaka</s> <s>Nandimitra</s> [Asv 119] said to King <s>Ajitasena</s> thus: 'So be it, great king — I shall partake of the alms-food in your house.' Then King <s>Ajitasena</s> satisfied that great <s>śrāvaka</s> <s>Nandimitra</s> with hard and soft foods.
Then the great <s>śrāvaka</s> <s>Nandimitra</s> said to King <s>Ajitasena</s> thus: 'Great king, is there a garden-ground in this region of yours?' The king replied: 'There is, O great <s>śrāvaka</s>, a garden-ground of mine, delightful and beautiful.' <s>Nandimitra</s> said: 'I shall go, great king, and inspect that garden-ground.' The king replied: 'Go, <s>Nandimitra</s>, and inspect the garden-ground.' Then the great <s>śrāvaka</s> <s>Nandimitra</s> approached the garden-ground of King <s>Ajitasena</s>. And in that garden-ground, all the qualities of a garden were present. The pools for summer were filled with cool water; those for the rainy season were filled with water neither too hot nor too cold. And those pools, covered with golden stairways, were divine and delightful. And all the pleasures of <s>Jambūdvīpa</s> were present. Flowers of <s>adhimukta</s>, <s>campaka</s>, <s>aśoka</s>, <s>mucilinda</s>, <s>pāṭala</s>, <s>sumanā</s>, and <s>saugandhika</s> were there. [Asv 120] Animals of various species — parrots, mynahs, <s>cakravāka</s> birds, peacocks, cuckoos, and others — uttered various sounds. And in that very garden-ground there appeared birds of golden color, with golden beaks, golden wings, and golden feet. They all uttered the word '<s>Buddha</s>.' Then the great <s>śrāvaka</s> <s>Nandimitra</s> returned to the royal capital of King <s>Ajitasena</s>. Then King <s>Ajitasena</s> said to the great <s>śrāvaka</s> <s>Nandimitra</s> thus: 'Have you returned, O great <s>śrāvaka</s>? Have you seen the garden-ground?' <s>Nandimitra</s> replied: 'I have seen the garden-ground — delightful and beautiful.' Then King <s>Ajitasena</s> addressed the great <s>śrāvaka</s> <s>Nandimitra</s> with verses:

children.translated_text: Whatever enjoyments exist in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> —
<s>adhimukta</s>, <s>campaka</s>, <s>dhānuṣkārikā</s> flowers,
<s>aśoka</s> and <s>mucilinda</s>, likewise <s>pāṭala</s>,
<s>saugandhika</s> and <s>sumanā</s>, blossoming in the rains —

body.text:
tadā pāriyātrā nadītīranirmitā
  suvarṇavarṇā sada pakṣiṇā abhūt* /

children.translated_text: they shall show the path to supreme awakening (<s>agrabodhi</s>),
divine and charming, with sweet voices,
and shall proclaim [the Dharma] constantly for all time.

body.translated_text: then, at the bank of the <s>Pāriyātra</s> river, there appeared birds of golden color always;

body.text:
atha nandimitramahāśrāvako rājño 'jitasenasya gāthā bhāṣitvā tūṣṇīṃ sthito 'bhūt* | atha rāja ajitaseno bherīṃ parāhante sma | (Asv 121) atha tena bherīśabdena sametyāmātyagaṇas taṃ rājānam ajitasenam evam āha | kasyārthe mahārāja bherī parāhatā | atha sa rājā āha | hastirathaṃ ca aśvarathaṃ ca sajjaṃ kṛtaṃ syāt* | aham udyānabhūmiṃ gamiṣyāmi krīḍanārthāya | atha tā amātyakoṭyo vacanaṃ śrutvā śīghram eva tad hastiratham aśvarathaṃ sajjaṃ kṛtavatyaḥ | atha tena kṣaṇalavamuhūrtamātreṇa rājājitaseno yena sodyānabhūmis tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | sa ca nandimitramahāśrāvakas tenaivopasaṃkrānto rājānam ajitasenam evam āha | asmin pṛthivīpradeśe mahārāja mama kuṭikaṃ kārayitavyaṃ yatrāhaṃ sanniṣaṇṇas tava gṛhe piṇḍapātaṃ paribhokṣyāmi | atha rājā ajitaseno nandimitramahāśrāvakam evam āha | kīdṛśaṃ tava kuṭikaṃ kārayitavyam* | nandimitra āha | yādṛśās tava mahārāja
mahācittotpādaśraddhāprasādās tādṛśaṃ kuṭikaṃ kāraya | atha rājā ajitaseno jyeṣṭhāmātyam evam āha | asminn eva pṛthivīpradeśe kuṭikaṃ kāraya | atha jyeṣṭhāmātyo rājānam evam āha | kīdṛśaṃ mahārāja kuṭikaṃ kārayāmi | rājā ajitasena evam āha | triṃśadyojanāni dīrgheṇa ṣaḍyojanāny ūrdhvāyāṃ saptaratnamayaṃ maṇimuktisaṃcchāditaṃ kuṭikaṃ kāraya | atha so 'mātyaḥ kuṭikaṃ kārayati | saptaratnamayaṃ (Asv 122) maṇimuktisaṃcchāditaṃ kārayitvā yena rājā ajitasenas tenopasaṃkrānto rājānam ajitasenam evam āha | kṛtaṃ mahārāja mayā kuṭikaṃ yādṛśam ājñaptam* | rājā āha | tatraiva pṛthivīpradeśe caṃkramaḥ kārayitavyaś caturyojanāni dīrgheṇa dve yojane vistāreṇa | atha so 'mātyas taṃ caṃkramaṃ kārayitvā yena rājā ajitasenas tenopasaṃkrānto rājānaṃ gāthābhir adhyabhāṣata |
body.translated_text: Then the great <s>śrāvaka</s> <s>Nandimitra</s>, having spoken the verse to King <s>Ajitasena</s>, stood in silence. Then King <s>Ajitasena</s> had a drum beaten. [Asv 121] Then, summoned by that drum-sound, the assembly of ministers said to King <s>Ajitasena</s> thus: 'For what purpose, great king, has the drum been beaten?' Then the king said: 'Let the elephant chariot and horse chariot be made ready. I shall go to the garden-ground for the purpose of amusement.' Then those tens of millions of ministers, having heard the command, very quickly made ready the elephant chariot and horse chariot. Then, in a mere instant, King <s>Ajitasena</s> approached that garden-ground. And the great <s>śrāvaka</s> <s>Nandimitra</s> also approached with him and said to King <s>Ajitasena</s> thus: 'In this region, great king, a hut (<s>kuṭika</s>) should be built for me, where I, seated, shall partake of alms-food from your house.' Then King <s>Ajitasena</s> said to the great <s>śrāvaka</s> <s>Nandimitra</s> thus: 'What kind of hut should be built for you?' <s>Nandimitra</s> replied: 'As great as are your aspirations of supreme faith, great king, so build the hut.' Then King <s>Ajitasena</s> said to his chief minister thus: 'In this very region, build a hut.' Then the chief minister said to the king thus: 'What kind of hut shall I build, great king?' King <s>Ajitasena</s> said thus: 'Build a hut thirty <s>yojanas</s> in length, six <s>yojanas</s> in height, made of the seven precious substances, and covered with gems and pearls.' Then that minister built the hut. [Asv 122] Having built it of the seven precious substances, covered with gems and pearls, he approached King <s>Ajitasena</s> and said thus: 'The hut has been built, great king, as commanded.' The king said: 'In that very region, a walking-terrace (<s>caṃkrama</s>) should be built — four <s>yojanas</s> in length, two <s>yojanas</s> in breadth.' Then that minister, having built the walking-terrace, approached King <s>Ajitasena</s> and addressed the king in verses:

children.translated_text: The walking-terrace has been built by me, well and beautifully,

children.text: ājñā tvayā yat kṛtapūrvam eva ca /
children.translated_text: as previously commanded by you.
It shall liberate beings from their nature of good and evil;
it shall free all living beings from this [suffering].
Oh, well-gained is the vow undertaken by you!
You shall liberate the whole world together with its gods.

children.text: praṇidhiṃ kṛtaṃ yat tvayam īdṛśaṃ bhave
children.translated_text: The vow that was made by you thus in this existence —
a preacher of <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmabhāṇaka</s>) shall illuminate the <s>Dharma</s> for me.
Whether seated or standing in the hut or on the walking-terrace —

children.text: ājñā kṛtaṃ yat tvaya yādṛśī kṛtā /
children.translated_text: whatever command was made by you, of whatever kind it was made,
the walking-terrace too has been made, well and beautiful,
that ground covered with gems and jewels.

body.text:
atha rājā ajitaseno yena svakā rājadhānī tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | atha nandimitramahāśrāvakaḥ pratinivṛtya tatraiva (Asv 123) kuṭike niṣaṇṇo vikiraṇaṃ nāma bodhisatvasamādhiṃ samāpanno 'bhūt* | anyena keśān anyena nayanāny anyena dantān anyena grīvā anyena bāhū anyena hṛdayam anyenodaram anyenorū anyena jaṅghe anyena pādau samāpanno 'bhūt* | atha sa rājā ajitasenaḥ saptāhasyātyayena taṃ bhikṣuṃ na paśyati |
atha rājā jyeṣṭhakumāram evam āha | āgaccha kulaputra gamiṣyāmi tāṃ kuṭikām* | yena sa bhikṣus tenopasaṃkramiṣyāmi | atha sa rājā saputro yena sā kuṭikā tenopasaṃkrānto 'bhūt* | atha sa rājā ajitasenas taṃ bhikṣum ātmabhāvaṃ khaṇḍaṃ khaṇḍaṃ kṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃśayajāto 'bhūt* | saṃtrastaromakūpajāto vastrāṇi pāṭayan paridevan rudan aśrukaṇṭhaḥ putram evam āha | ānaya putra tīkṣṇadhāram asim* | ātmānaṃ jīvitād vyavaropayiṣyāmi | atha sa rājakumāraḥ prāṃjaliṃ kṛtvā rājānaṃ gāthābhir adhyabhāṣata |
body.translated_text:
Then King <s>Ajitasena</s> returned to his own royal capital. Then the great <s>śrāvaka</s> <s>Nandimitra</s>, having returned, seated himself [Asv 123] in that very hut and entered the <s>bodhisattva samādhi</s> called <s>Vikiraṇa</s> (Dispersion). By one [part of his body he manifested as] his hair, by another his eyes, by another his teeth, by another his neck, by another his arms, by another his heart, by another his belly, by another his thighs, by another his shins, by another his feet — thus he entered [the samādhi, dispersing his body]. Then King <s>Ajitasena</s>, after seven days had passed, did not see that monk.
Then the king said to his eldest prince thus: 'Come, son of good family — I shall go to that hut. I shall approach where that monk is.' Then the king, together with his son, approached that hut. Then King <s>Ajitasena</s>, seeing that monk's body cut into piece after piece, became filled with doubt. With the hair of his body standing on end from terror, tearing his garments, lamenting, weeping, with tear-choked voice, he said to his son: 'Bring me, son, a sharp-edged sword! I shall take my own life.' Then the prince, with palms joined, addressed the king in verses:

children.translated_text: Do not be of grieving mind, O lord of men!
Do not experience such anguish!

children.text: ātmaghātaṃ karitvā tu niraye tvaṃ gamiṣyasi
children.translated_text: Having committed self-slaughter, you will go to hell —
to the terrible <s>Raurava</s> hell you will go!

body.text: ... dakṣiṇīyo ayaṃ loke jaravyādhipramocakaḥ / (Asv 124)
body.translated_text: ...He is worthy of offerings in this world, a liberator from old age and disease. [Asv 124]

children.text: na cāyaṃ ghātito yakṣair na bhūtair na ca rākṣasaiḥ /
children.translated_text: He has not been slain by <s>yakṣas</s>, nor by <s>bhūtas</s>, nor by <s>rākṣasas</s>;
he is a <s>bodhisattva</s> in this world, a liberator from old age and disease.
He is worthy of offerings in this world, a liberator from old age and disease;
his sight is hard to obtain — he is one who shows the path to awakening.

children.text: kalyāṇamitram ayaṃ āsī tava kāraṇam āgatam* /
children.translated_text: He was your spiritual friend (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>), who came for your sake;
he is worthy of offerings in this world — [bringing] happiness to all beings.
He who has attained omniscience and the perfections (<s>pāramī</s>), sent by the Lord of the World;
of firm vigor and firm strength — the Lord of the World, the great sage.

children.text: yo nāma tasya dhāreti nāsau gacchati durgatim* /
children.translated_text: Whoever bears his name shall not go to an evil destiny;
they shall not go to the lower realms, [but] shall be reborn in the heavenly world.

body.text:
atha sa rājakumāras taṃ pitaraṃ gāthā bhāṣitvā tūṣṇīṃ sthito 'bhūt* | atha rājā ajitasenaḥ svakaṃ putram evam āha | kathaṃ tvaṃ kumāra jānīṣe yad ayaṃ bhikṣuḥ samādhiṃ samāpanno 'bhūt* | atha sa rājakumāra evam āha | paśya mahārāja ayaṃ bhikṣur bodhisatvasamādhiṃ samāpannaḥ sarvakleśavinirmukto bhavasāgarapāraṃgataḥ sarvasatvahitārthaṃ ca mārgaṃ darśayate śubham* | atha sa rājakumāro rājānam evam āha | āgaccha tāta caṃkramaṃ gamiṣyāmaḥ | atha sa rājā sa ca rājakumāro bahubhir dārakaśataiḥ sārdhaṃ yena sa caṃkramas tenopasaṃkrāntau | atha sa bhikṣus tataḥ samādher vyutthito rājānam ajitasenam evam āha | āgaccha mahārāja kiṃ karoṣy asmin sthāne | (Asv 125)
atha rājā taṃ bhikṣuṃ dṛṣṭvā maulipaṭṭaṃ rājakumārasya dadāti | tava rājyaṃ bhavatu | dharmeṇa pālaye nādharmeṇa | rājakumāra āha | bahūny asaṃkhyeyāni rājakāryāṇi mayā kṛtāni | na ca kadācit tṛptir āsīt* | tava tāta rājyaṃ bhavatu | na mama rājyena kāryaṃ na bhogena naiśvaryādhipatyena kāryam* | tava rājyaṃ bhavatu tāta | dharmeṇa pālaye nādharmeṇeti |
atha rājā yena sa bhikṣus tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ prāñjalir evam āha |

children.translated_text: 'Most rare is the sight of you, O holy one;
with palms joined, face to face with the Leaders —'
'The approach to liberation is your teaching, O holy one;
most rare [to obtain] through hundreds of inconceivable <s>karmas</s>!'

body.translated_text:
Then that prince, having spoken verses to his father, remained silent. Then King <s>Ajitasena</s> said to his own son: 'How do you know, O prince, that this monk has entered <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption)?' Then that prince said: 'Behold, O great king! This monk has entered the <s>Bodhisattva-samādhi</s>; he is freed from all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), has gone beyond the ocean of existence, and shows the auspicious path for the welfare of all beings.' Then that prince said to the king: 'Come, father, let us go to the walking-path.' Then that king and that prince, together with many hundreds of boys, approached that walking-path. Then that monk, having arisen from that <s>samādhi</s>, said to King <s>Ajitasena</s>: 'Come, O great king! What are you doing in this place?'
Then the king, seeing that monk, gave the crown-band to the prince [saying]: 'The kingdom shall be yours. Rule with <s>Dharma</s>, not with <s>adharma</s>.' The prince said: 'Innumerable royal duties have been performed by me, yet never was there satisfaction. The kingdom shall be yours, father. I have no need of kingship, nor of enjoyments, nor of sovereign authority. The kingdom shall be yours, father. Rule with <s>Dharma</s>, not with <s>adharma</s>.'
Then the king approached that monk and said with palms joined:

children.translated_text: 'He who shall give you a sight, O holy one —'
'that one shall be freed for <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>!'
'Never shall one go to the downfall of misfortune'
'who hears [your] name even for a moment!'

body.text: rājā āha |
body.translated_text: The king said:

body.text:
niṣadya yugye ratanāmaye śubhe
  vrajāmy ahaṃ yena sa rājadhānīm* /
dadāmy ahaṃ bhojanu suprabhūtaṃ
  dadāmy ahaṃ kāśikavastram etat* /

children.translated_text: 'And fine nets assembled together —'
'these robes I give to you today!'

body.translated_text:
'Seated upon a beautiful jeweled chariot,
I shall go to the royal capital.
I shall give abundant food;
I shall give this <s>Kāśi</s> garment!'

body.text: atha sa bhikṣū ratnamaye yugye gṛhītvā yena rājadhānī tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ / santarpito bhojanena / atha nandimitramahāśrāvako rājānam ajitasenaṃ gāthābhir adhyabhāṣata |
body.translated_text: Then that monk, having been placed in the jeweled chariot, approached the royal capital. He was satisfied with food. Then the great disciple <s>Nandimitra</s> addressed King <s>Ajitasena</s> in verses:

children.translated_text: 'Satisfied with abundant food,
with delicious food, drink, and flavors, the highest and auspicious —'
'Those who give gifts to the <s>Bhikṣu-saṃgha</s> (community of monks)'
'they go to the seat of awakening (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>) before long!'
'Most rare is the sight of the Leader —'
'before long, that one goes to the Buddha-field!'
'In the excellent Buddha-field of <s>Amitāyus</s> —'
'one goes quickly to <s>Sukhāvatī</s>!'

body.text:
atha nandimitramahāśrāvakaḥ ajitasenasya rājño gāthā bhāṣitvā tūṣṇīṃ sthito 'bhūt* | atha rājā ajitaseno bherīṃ parāhanti sma | atha tena bherīśabdena sarvās tā amātyakoṭyo rājānam evam āhuḥ | kasyārthe mahārāja bherī parāhatā | rājā āha | saptame divase hastiratham aśvarathaṃ sajjaṃ kṛtaṃ syāt* | ahaṃ saptame divase jetavanaṃ nāma vihāraṃ gamiṣyāmi śākyamunes tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya darśanāya vandanāya paryupāsanāya dharmaśravaṇāya (Asv 127) | athāmātyakoṭyas taṃ rājānam ajitasenam evam āhuḥ | kṛtam asmābhiḥ mahārāja hastiratham aśvarathaṃ sajjam* | atha rājā ajitaseno hastirathe avaruhya taṃ ca nandimitramahāśrāvakaṃ ratnamaye rathe avarohya yena jetavanaṃ vihāras tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | atha bhagavān rājānam ajitasenaṃ dūrata evāgacchantaṃ dṛṣṭvā tān sarvaśrāvakān āmantrayata | sarvair nānāṛddhivikurvitaṃ darśayitavyam* | atha te sarve mahāśrāvakā
jvālāmālaṃ nāma bodhisatvasamādhiṃ samāpannā abhūvan* | atha rājā dūratas taṃ jvālāmālaṃ dṛṣṭvā nandimitramahāśrāvakam evam āha | kasyārthe imaṃ parvataṃ jvālāmālībhūtaṃ paśyāmi | nandimitra āha | atra śākyamunis tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sthitiṃ dhriyate yāpayati dharmaṃ ca deśayati | te ca bodhisatvā jvālāmālaṃ nāma bodhisatvasamādhiṃ samāpannāḥ | atha rājā ajitaseno hastirathād avatīrya pādābhyāṃ putrasahasreṇa sārdhaṃ yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | atha bhagavān suvarṇavarṇena kāyena vyāmaprabhayā caṃkramate sma | atha rājā ajitaseno bhagavato rūpavarṇaliṃgasaṃsthānaṃ dṛṣṭvā mūrcchitvā dharaṇitale nipatitaḥ | atha bhagavān suvarṇavarṇaṃ bāhuṃ prasārya taṃ rājānam utthāpayati sma | uttiṣṭha mahārāja kasyārthe prapatitaḥ | rājā aha | (Asv 128)
body.translated_text: Then the great disciple <s>Nandimitra</s>, having spoken verses to King <s>Ajitasena</s>, remained silent. Then King <s>Ajitasena</s> struck the drum. Then, by that drum-sound, all those <s>koṭis</s> of ministers said to the king: 'For what purpose, O great king, was the drum struck?' The king said: 'On the seventh day, let the elephant-chariot and horse-chariot be prepared. On the seventh day, I shall go to the <s>Jetavana</s> monastery for the sight, worship, attendance, and hearing of the <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Tathāgata Śākyamuni</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly enlightened Buddha.' Then the <s>koṭis</s> of ministers said to King <s>Ajitasena</s>: 'It is done, O great king; the elephant-chariot and horse-chariot are prepared.' Then King <s>Ajitasena</s>, descending from the elephant-chariot and placing that great disciple <s>Nandimitra</s> in the jeweled chariot, approached the <s>Jetavana</s> monastery. Then the Blessed One, seeing King <s>Ajitasena</s> approaching from afar, addressed all those disciples: 'All must display various miraculous transformations!' Then all those great disciples entered the <s>Bodhisattva-samādhi</s> called <s>Jvālāmāla</s> (Garland of Flames). Then the king, seeing that <s>Jvālāmāla</s> from afar, said to the great disciple <s>Nandimitra</s>: 'For what reason do I see this mountain become a garland of flames?' <s>Nandimitra</s> said: 'Here the <s>Tathāgata Śākyamuni</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly enlightened Buddha, abides, dwells, and teaches the <s>Dharma</s>. And those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> have entered the <s>Bodhisattva-samādhi</s> called <s>Jvālāmāla</s>.' Then King <s>Ajitasena</s>, descending from the elephant-chariot, on foot, together with his thousand sons, approached the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One walked about with his golden-colored body and the radiance of a fathom's length. Then King <s>Ajitasena</s>, having seen the form, color, appearance, and shape of the Blessed One, fainted and fell to the ground.

children.translated_text: 'For many inconceivable <s>kalpas</s>,
for inconceivable hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of births —'
'never before have I seen such a form!'
'You are the Lord of the World, the best recipient of offerings!'

atha rājā ajitasenaḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ bhagavantam evam āha | ahaṃ bhagavan tava śāsane pravrajiṣyāmi | atha bhagavān tuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumansyajātaḥ | alabdhalābhā ye [tatra] mama śāsanaṃ vaistārikaṃ bhavati | taṃ rājānam ajitasenam evam āha | gaccha tvaṃ mahārāja svagṛhe saptame divase āgamiṣyāmi |
atha rājā ajitasenas tuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumansyajātas taṃ kalyāṇamitraṃ bhikṣuṃ purataḥsthāpya svagṛhaṃ gatvā sarvān amātyān āmantrayate sma | sarvair grāmanagaranigamajanapadaiḥ pathaṃ śodhayitavyaṃ gṛhe gṛhe dhvajāny ucchrāpitavyāni gṛhe gṛhe ratnamayāni (Asv 129) kumbhāni paripūrayitavyāni | tadā taiḥ sarvair amātyair ājñātam* | sarvagrāmanagaranigamajanapadaiḥ pathaṃ śodhitaṃ dhvajāny ucchrāpitāni ratnamayāni kumbhāni paripūritāni | yatra rājā ajitasenaḥ prativasati tatra dvādaśakoṭyo dhvajānām ucchrāpitā dvādaśakoṭyo ratnamayānāṃ kumbhānāṃ paripūritāḥ | yāvat saptame divase tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ śāriputramaudgalyāyanānandapūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputrapramukhair mahāśrāvakasaṃghaiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛtaḥ ajitasenasya rājño rājadhānīm anuprāptaḥ | atha rājā ajitasenaḥ puṣpapiṭakaṃ gṛhītvā kalyāṇamitraṃ purataḥsthāpya
bhagavantaṃ puṣpair avakiran bhagavantam evam āha |
anena kuśalamūlena sarvasatvā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisampadyante | atha rājñā ajitasenena āsanāni prajñaptāni | tasya bhagavataḥ siṃhāsanaṃ pradattam* | atha bhagavān siṃhāsane niṣaṇṇo rājño 'jitasenasya dharmān deśitavān* | atha rājñā ajitasenena prabhūtenāhāreṇa khādanīyena bhojanīyena santarpitaḥ | atha rājā ajitaseno jyeṣṭhakaṃ rājakumāraṃ dadāti | imaṃ rājakumāraṃ pravrājaya | tad ahaṃ paścāt pravrajiṣyāmi | atha bhagavān āyuṣmantam ānandam āmantrayate sma | gacchānanda imaṃ rājakumāraṃ pravrājaya | (Asv 130) athāyuṣmatānandena sa rājakumāraḥ pravrājitaḥ | saha pravrajitamātreṇa arhatphalaṃ prāptam abhūt* | sarvabuddhakṣetrāṇi paśyati sma | atha sa rājakumāro 'ntarīkṣagatas taṃ pitaraṃ gāthābhir adhyabhāṣata |

Then King <s>Ajitasena</s>, with palms joined, said to the Blessed One: 'I, O Blessed One, shall go forth [as a monk] in your teaching.' Then the Blessed One was pleased, elated, delighted, joyful, filled with joy and gladness: 'Well-gained is the gain for those where my teaching spreads widely!' He said to King <s>Ajitasena</s>: 'Go, O great king, to your home. On the seventh day, I shall come.'
Then King <s>Ajitasena</s>, pleased, elated, delighted, joyful, filled with joy and gladness, placing that virtuous friend the monk at the front, went to his home and addressed all the ministers: 'By all the villages, towns, market-towns, and districts, the road is to be cleaned; in every house, banners are to be raised; in every house, jeweled vessels are to be filled!' Then all those ministers understood the order. By all the villages, towns, market-towns, and districts, the road was cleaned, banners were raised, jeweled vessels were filled. Where King <s>Ajitasena</s> dwelt, twelve <s>koṭis</s> of banners were raised [and] twelve <s>koṭis</s> of jeweled vessels were filled. On the seventh day, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly enlightened Buddha, surrounded and preceded by the great disciple communities led by <s>Śāriputra</s>, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, <s>Pūrṇa Maitrāyaṇīputra</s>, arrived at the royal capital of King <s>Ajitasena</s>. Then King <s>Ajitasena</s>, taking a basket of flowers, placing the virtuous friend at the front, scattered flowers upon the Blessed One and said to the Blessed One:
'By this root of merit, may all beings attain supreme, perfect awakening!' Then, by King <s>Ajitasena</s>, seats were prepared. To the Blessed One, a lion-throne was offered. Then the Blessed One, seated upon the lion-throne, taught the <s>Dharma</s> to King <s>Ajitasena</s>. Then, by King <s>Ajitasena</s>, with abundant food —

children.translated_text: 'Do not delay, father!'
'Do not be troubled in any way!'
'Ah, how well-gained is the sight of the <s>Sugatas</s> (Buddhas)!'
Oh, well-gained is the gain of the <s>Sugatas</s>!
Oh, well-gained is the supreme gain—
the gain of going forth, praised by the <s>Sugata</s>;
liberation from <s>saṃsāra</s>, proclaimed by the <s>Sugata</s>—
go forth quickly, do not delay, dear father!

body.text:
mā khedayī lokavināyakendraṃ

...sudurlabhaṃ darśanu nāyakānām* /

children.translated_text: Go forth quickly; by me it has been gained—
I have attained the supreme, foremost <s>bodhi</s> (awakening)!"
Having heard the words of his son, the king
went forth in the teaching of the Leader.

body.translated_text: Do not cause grief to the chief Leader of the World; you have obtained the rarely obtained human birth. Rarely obtained is the sight of the Leaders.

atha rājakumāro 'ntarīkṣagato gāthāṃ bhāṣitva tūṣṇīṃ sthito 'bhūt* | atha rājā ajitasenaḥ putrasya vākyaṃ śrutvā tuṣṭa udagra (Asv 131) āttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ [prīti]saumansyajāto bhagavantam uddiśya vihāraṃ kārayati sma | tūryakoṭyo 'nupradattāḥ | antaḥpurasahasram asyāstrīndriyam antarhitapuruṣendriyaṃ prādurabhūt* | atha rājā ajitaseno bhagavataḥ śāsane pravrajito 'bhūt* | tāś cāmātyakoṭyo bhagavataḥ śāsane pravrajitā abhūvan* | tac cāntaḥpurapuruṣasahasraṃ pravrajitam abhūt* | bhagavān rājānam ajitasenaṃ pravrājya yena jetavanaṃ vihāras tena gamanam ārabdhavān* |
athāyuṣmān ānando bhagavantam evam āha | ayaṃ rājā ajitaseno rājyaṃ parityajya vihāraṃ kārayitvā bhagavataḥ śāsane pravrajito 'bhūt* | asya kīdṛśaṃ kuśalamūlaṃ bhaviṣyati | bhagavān āha | sādhu sādhu ānanda yat tvayā parikīrtitam* | ayaṃ rājā ajitaseno mama śāsane pravrajito bhaviṣyati | anāgate 'dhvany aparimitaiḥ kalpair acintyair aparimāṇair ajitaprabho nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho loke bhaviṣyati vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān* | ānanda āha | ayaṃ nandimitramahāśrāvako rājñaḥ kalyāṇamitram abhūt* | kīdṛśaṃ vāsya kuśalamūlaṃ bhaviṣyati | bhagavān āha | (Asv 132) ayam ānanda nandimitramahāśrāvakas tatraiva kālasamaye nandiprabho nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho loke bhaviṣyati | ānanda āha | kīdṛśaṃ bhagavan* teṣāṃ tathāgatānāṃ buddhakṣetraṃ bhaviṣyati | bhagavān
āha | aparimitaguṇasaṃcayā nāma sā buddhakṣetraṃ bhaviṣyati yatreme tathāgatā bhaviṣyanti | ānanda āha | ya imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ sakalaṃ samāptaṃ paścime kāle paścime samaye saṃprakāśayiṣyati tasya kīdṛśaḥ puṇyaskandho bhaviṣyati | bhagavān āha | yadā mayānanda duṣkarakoṭiniyutaśatasahasrāṇi caritvā bodhir abhisaṃbuddhā tadā te satvā bodhim abhisaṃbhotsyante | ya etaddharmaparyāyāt* catuṣpadikām api gāthāṃ śroṣyanti avaivartikāś ca te satvā bhaviṣyanty anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau | ānanda āha | ya imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ dharmabhāṇakāḥ saṃprakāśayiṣyanti teṣāṃ kīdṛśaṃ kuśalamūlaṃ bhaviṣyati | bhagavān āha | śṛṇu ānanda rājā bhaviṣyati cakravartī caturdvīpeśvaraḥ | ya imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ sakalaṃ samāptaṃ saṃprakāśayiṣyanti muktāś ca bhaviṣyanti jātijarāvyādhiparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsebhyaḥ parimuktā bhaviṣyanti | ānanda āha
| ye paścime kāle paścime samaye satvā imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ pratikṣepsyanti na pattīyiṣyanti teṣāṃ kā gatir bhaviṣyati kaḥ parāyaṇam* | (Asv 133) bhagavān āha | alam alam ānanda | mā me pāpakaṃ karmaskandhaṃ paripṛccha | na mayā śakyaṃ parikīrtayitum* | anyatra buddhakoṭibhir na śakyaṃ parikīrtayitum* | ānanda āha | parikīrtaya bhagavan parikīrtaya | sugato bhagavān āha | śṛṇu ānanda saddharmapratikṣepakasya gatiṃ parikīrtayiṣyāmi | raurave mahānarake hāhahe mahānarake avīcau mahānarake tiryagyonau yamaloke ca pretaviṣaye bahūni kalpasahasrāṇi duḥkham anubhavitavyam* | yadi kadācin manuṣyaloke upapatsyate dīrghaśuṣkatālukaṇṭho bhaviṣyati | dvādaśayojanāni tasya jihvā bhaviṣyati | dvādaśahalyāni pravahiṣyanti ye evaṃ vāg bhāṣiṣyante | mā bhoḥ kulaputrā bhoḥ kvacit saddharmaṃ pratikṣepsyatha | saddharmapratikṣepakasya evaṃ gatir bhavati | ānanda āha | kena hetunā bhagavan saddharmaḥ
pratikṣipto bhavati | bhagavān āha | ye satvāḥ paścime kāle paścime samaye eteṣāṃ sūtrānudhārakāṇāṃ dharmabhāṇakānām ākrośiṣyanti paribhāṣiṣyante kutsayiṣyanti paṃsayiṣyanti tasya dharmabhāṇakasya duṣṭacittam utpādayiṣyanti tebhyaḥ saddharmaḥ pratikṣipto bhaviṣyati | yaḥ satvaḥ (Asv 134) trisāhasramahāsāhasryāṃ lokadhātau satvānām akṣīṇy utpāṭayet* ayaṃ tato bahutaram apuṇyaskandho bhavet* | evam eva ya eteṣāṃ sūtradhārakāṇāṃ dharmabhāṇakānāṃ duṣṭacittaprekṣitā ayaṃ tato bahutaram apuṇyaskandhaṃ prasaviṣyate |
atha ānando bhagavato gāthāḥ pratyabhāṣata |
body.translated_text: Then the prince, having spoken the verse while standing in the sky, fell silent. Then King <s>Ajitasena</s>, having heard his son's words, became pleased, elated, delighted, joyful, and filled with delight and happiness. Directing his thoughts toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, he had a monastery built. Tens of millions of musical instruments were offered. His inner palace of a thousand women—their female faculty disappeared and the male faculty appeared. Then King <s>Ajitasena</s> went forth in the <s>Bhagavān's</s> teaching. Those tens of millions of ministers went forth in the <s>Bhagavān's</s> teaching. And that thousand of the inner palace went forth. The <s>Bhagavān</s>, having ordained King <s>Ajitasena</s>, set out toward the <s>Jetavana</s> monastery. Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> thus: 'This King <s>Ajitasena</s>, having renounced his kingdom and had a monastery built, went forth in the <s>Bhagavān's</s> teaching. What wholesome root will be his?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Well done, well done, <s>Ānanda</s>, that you have asked. This King <s>Ajitasena</s>, having gone forth in my teaching, in the future, after immeasurable and inconceivable aeons, will become a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Ajitaprabha</s> (Invincible Radiance), an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s> in the world, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, a Knower of the World, an unsurpassed charioteer of men to be tamed, a Teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Bhagavān</s>.' <s>Ānanda</s> said: 'This great <s>śrāvaka</s> <s>Nandimitra</s> was the king's spiritual friend. What wholesome root will be his?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'This <s>Nandimitra</s>, the great <s>śrāvaka</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, at that very time, will become a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Nandiprabha</s> (Joyful Radiance), an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s> in the world.' <s>Ānanda</s> said: 'What, <s>Bhagavān</s>, will be the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field) of those <s>Tathāgatas</s>?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'That <s>buddhakṣetra</s> will be called <s>Aparimitaguṇasaṃcaya</s> (Accumulation of Immeasurable Virtues), where those <s>Tathāgatas</s> will appear.' <s>Ānanda</s> said: 'For one who will illuminate this entire, complete <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse on <s>Dharma</s>) in the final time, in the final period—what accumulation of merit will there be?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'When, <s>Ānanda</s>, through the practice of tens of millions of hundreds of thousands of austerities, <s>bodhi</s> has been attained by me, then those beings will attain awakening. Those who hear even a single four-line verse from this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> will become non-retrogressing from unsurpassed perfect awakening.' <s>Ānanda</s> said: 'For those <s>dharmabhāṇakas</s> (preachers of <s>Dharma</s>) who will illuminate this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>, what wholesome root will there be?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Listen, <s>Ānanda</s>. He will become a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch) king, lord of the four continents. Those who illuminate this complete <s>dharmaparyāya</s> will be liberated—freed from birth, old age, disease, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair.' <s>Ānanda</s> said: 'For those beings who in the final time, in the final period, will reject this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> and not believe in it—what destiny will be theirs, and what their future state?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Enough, enough, <s>Ānanda</s>! Do not ask me about evil accumulations of <s>karma</s>. It is not possible for me to proclaim them. Even billions of <s>Buddhas</s> cannot proclaim them.' <s>Ānanda</s> said: 'Please proclaim it, <s>Bhagavān</s>, please proclaim it, <s>Sugata</s>!' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Listen, <s>Ānanda</s>, I shall proclaim the destiny of one who rejects the true <s>Dharma</s>. In the <s>Raurava</s> great hell, in the <s>Hāhaha</s> great hell, in the <s>Avīci</s> great hell, in the animal realm, in the world of <s>Yama</s>, and in the <s>preta</s> (hungry ghost) realm, one must experience suffering for many thousands of aeons. If by chance one is reborn in the human world, one will have a dry, parched throat twelve <s>yojanas</s> long, and one's tongue will be twelve <s>yojanas</s> in length. Twelve plows will go over it. Such words shall be spoken: "Do not, O sons of good family, ever reject the true <s>Dharma</s>! Such is the destiny of one who rejects the true <s>Dharma</s>."' <s>Ānanda</s> said: 'For what reason, <s>Bhagavān</s>, is the true <s>Dharma</s> rejected?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Those beings who in the final time, in the final period, will abuse, revile, disparage, and slander those <s>dharmabhāṇakas</s> who uphold these <s>sūtras</s>, and generate an evil mind toward those preachers of <s>Dharma</s>—by them the true <s>Dharma</s> is rejected. If a being were to gouge out the eyes of all beings in the great trichiliocosm, this would produce a great accumulation of demerit. But one who looks with evil intent at these upholders of <s>sūtras</s>, the preachers of <s>Dharma</s>, will produce a far greater accumulation of demerit than that.' Then <s>Ānanda</s> spoke verses to the <s>Bhagavān</s>:

body.text:
bahusūtrasahasrāṇi $ śrutaṃ me śāstusaṃmukhāt* &
na [ca] me īdṛśaṃ sūtraṃ % śrutapūrvaṃ kadācana //
body.translated_text: "Many thousands of <s>sūtras</s> have I heard in the presence of the Teacher; but never have I heard a <s>sūtra</s> like this before.

body.text:
parinirvṛtasya śāstusya $ paścātkāle subhairave &
idaṃ sūtraṃ prakāśiṣye % dhārayiṣye imaṃ nayam* //
body.translated_text: After the Teacher has passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, in the future time, in the fearful age, I shall illuminate this <s>sūtra</s> and uphold this teaching.

body.text:
yatra sūtraratne asmiṃ $ paścātkāle bhaviṣyati &
rakṣāṃ kariṣyāmi teṣāṃ % paścātkale subhairave //
body.translated_text: Wherever this jewel of a <s>sūtra</s> shall exist in the future time, I shall provide protection for those [who uphold it] in the future, in the fearful age.

body.text: pratikṣipiṣyāmi nedaṃ $ gaṃbhīraṃ buddhabhāṣitam* //
body.translated_text: I shall not reject this profound word of the <s>Buddha</s>."

body.text: athāyuṣmān ānando bhagavato gāthā bhāṣitvā tūṣṇīṃ sthito 'bhūt* | atha kāśyapo mahāśrāvako bhagavantaṃ gāthābhir adhyabhāṣata |
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having spoken verses to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, stood in silence. Then the great <s>śrāvaka</s> <s>Kāśyapa</s> addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> in verses:

children.translated_text: "The <s>Jina</s> (Victor) of golden complexion, with excellent marks and limbs,
bearing the thirty-two marks;
well-spoken is this <s>sūtra</s> of great power,
of profound <s>Dharma</s>, subtle, and hard to see.

body.text:
(Asv 135)
prakāśitaṃ sūtram idaṃ niruttaraṃ
  mā paścakāle parinirvṛte jine /
dhāriṣye maṃ sūtranayaṃ niruttaraṃ /
body.translated_text: This unsurpassed <s>sūtra</s> has been illuminated; after the <s>Jina</s> has passed away in the future time, I shall uphold this unsurpassed <s>sūtra</s> teaching."

body.text: athāyuṣmān* śāradvatīputro bhagavantaṃ gāthābhir adhyabhāṣata /
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> (Śāriputra) addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> in verses:

children.translated_text: "Homage to you, O <s>Buddha</s> of great power!
This unsurpassed <s>sūtra</s> has been illuminated.
After you, O Leader of the World, have passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>,
they shall write down this unsurpassed <s>sūtra</s>.

body.text:
na cāpi so gacchati durgatībhayaṃ
  svargaṃ ca so gacchati kṣipram etat* //
body.translated_text: One who does so shall not go to the fearful lower realms, and shall quickly go to heaven."

body.text: athāyuṣmān pūrṇo maitrāyaṇīputro bhagavantaṃ gāthābhir adhyabhāṣata |
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Pūrṇa Maitrāyaṇīputra</s> addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> in verses:

body.text:
kṛtajño bahusatvānāṃ $ mocako durgatībhayāt* &
prakāśitaṃ tvayā sūtraṃ % gambhīraṃ buddhadakṣiṇam* //
body.translated_text: "Grateful to many beings, liberator from the fear of lower realms, you have illuminated this <s>sūtra</s>, profound, worthy of the <s>Buddha</s>.

ahaṃ hi paścime kāle $ nirvṛte tvayi nāyake &
idaṃ sūtraṃ prakāśiṣye % hitāya sarvaprāṇinām* //
body.translated_text: I, in the future time, when you, the Leader, have passed into <s>nirvāṇa</s>, shall illuminate this <s>sūtra</s> for the benefit of all living beings."

body.text: iti
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: atha brahmā sahāṃpatir bhagavantaṃ gāthābhir adhyabhāṣata |
body.translated_text: Then <s>Brahmā Sahāṃpati</s> addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> in verses:

body.text:
namo 'stu te buddha mahānubhāvā
  prakāśitaṃ sūtram idaṃ tvayā śubham* /

children.translated_text: After you, O Leader of the World, have passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>,
I shall provide protection for this jewel of a <s>sūtra</s>."

body.translated_text: "Homage to you, O <s>Buddha</s> of great power! You have illuminated this auspicious <s>sūtra</s>.

body.text: atha catvāro mahārājā bhagavantaṃ gāthābhir adhyabhāṣanta |
body.translated_text: Then the Four Great Kings addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> in verses:

children.translated_text: "Oh, how delightful is this excellent jewel of a <s>sūtra</s>,
illuminated thus in the future time!
... this jewel of a <s>sūtra</s>,
illuminated for those who shall see it in the future time.
Of the <s>Sugatas</s>, the Leaders of the World—
we shall uphold the jewel of a <s>sūtra</s>;
I shall provide protection for this jewel of a <s>sūtra</s>."
This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said, delighted.

children.text: sā ca sarvāvatī parṣad bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandat* /
children.translated_text: And that entire assembly rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān's</s> words.
The <s>Mahāyānasūtra</s> called <s>Ajitasenavyākaraṇanirdeśa</s> (Instruction on the Prophecy of <s>Ajitasena</s>) is completed.

body.text: deyadharmo 'yaṃ bālosiṃhena sārdhaṃ bhāryājājatitrana sārdhaṃ mātāpitroḥ paramaduṣkartroḥ sārdhaṃ kṣiṇīena akhiloṭiena diśoṭajāja maṃgali ... utrayannagarvidoṭiena vaṭrari-khuśoṭi-khuśogoṭiena sārdhaṃ sarvasatvaiḥ sarva ... bhir yatra puṇya tadbha ... sarvasatvānām anuttaraḥ ... sārdhaṃ paramakalyāṇamitrasthirabandhuena | likhitam idaṃ pustakaṃ dharmabhāṇakanarendradattena |
body.translated_text: This is the pious gift of <s>Bālosiṃha</s>, together with [his] wife <s>Jājatitrana</s>, together with [his] parents, the most difficult to repay, together with <s>Kṣiṇī</s>, <s>Akhiloṭi</s>, <s>Diśoṭajāja</s>, <s>Maṅgali</s> ... <s>Utrayannagarvidoṭi</s>, <s>Vaṭrari</s>-<s>Khuśoṭi</s>-<s>Khuśogoṭi</s>, together with all beings, all ... whatever merit [there is], may it be ... for all beings, the unsurpassed ... together with the excellent spiritual friend <s>Sthirabandhu</s>. This manuscript was written by the <s>Dharma</s>-reciter <s>Narendradatta</s>.
